The source text explicitly states that among 15 pediatric and young adult patients (<22 years) with solid tumors harboring NTRK1, NTRK2, or NTRK3 fusions, entrectinib demonstrated a confirmed objective response rate (ORR) of 60.0% (9/15). This directly validates the efficacy (sensitivity/response) of entrectinib in the specified molecularly defined population (NTRK1/2/3 fusions) across the specified age ranges (pediatric and young adult onset). The other roles (timeline, genomics, pathology) were marked as not_applicable due to missing input, but the core clinical efficacy claim is substantiated by the literature and drug roles, which were confirmed by the verifier.

citations.quote: In the STARTRK-NG (NCT02650401) phase 1/2 trial, 43 pediatric and young adult patients (age <22 years) with recurrent or refractory solid tumors, including primary CNS tumors, were evaluated for response to entrectinib. The study enrolled patients with or without *NTRK1/2/3*, ROS1, or ALK fusions. Among the 15 patients with *NTRK1/2/3* fusions (4 NTRK1, 4 NTRK2, 7 NTRK3), the confirmed objective response rate (ORR) by blinded independent review was 60.0% (9/15; 95% CI 32.3-83.7). Responses in this group were observed in 5 of 11 patients with primary CNS tumors and all 4 patients with

extracranial solid tumors. In contrast, the non-fusion population (n = 17) had an investigator-assessed ORR of 5.9% (1/17; 95% CI 0.15-28.7), which was a single complete response in a neuroblastoma patient with an ALK F1174L point mutation. The authors conclude that entrectinib resulted in rapid and durable responses in pediatric patients with solid tumors harboring *NTRK1/2/3* fusions.
